Peel Region confirms West Nile virus found in mosquitoes: What you need to know
items.summary: The first West Nile virus case this year has been confirmed in Peel Region. The mosquitoes were identified in Brampton near the intersection of Queen Street East and Kennedy Road North. With the virus now active locally, residents are advised to take steps to protect themselves (and their property) from infected insects. What is West Nile virus? West Nile virus is a mosquito-borne illness that can cause mild flu-like symptoms in most people, but in rare cases, it can lead to serious illness affecting the brain or nervous system.

items.title: Public engagements open in August
items.summary: The City of Mississauga regularly connects with residents throughout the year to gather their ideas and constructive feedback. This helps guide City plans, programs, services and new developments. Residents and businesses can take part in different ways. You can participate by attending information sessions, open houses and workshops or completing online surveys. The City reviews this feedback along with other data and trends to help decide how to focus its time and resources on community priorities.

items.title: Voting in the 2026 Municipal Election? Check the voters’ list
items.summary: Mississauga’s 2026 Municipal Election is on Monday, October 26. Eligible voters will elect Mississauga’s Mayor, their Ward/Regional Councillor and School Board Trustees for the 2026–2030 term of office. Use the Voter Registration Portal to check, update or add your information to the voters’ list before voting begins. Being on the voters’ list helps confirm you’re eligible to vote, helps ensure you receive a Voter notification card and can make the process faster when you arrive to vote.
